coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no partition, no Region-availability table, and no 'available in the following Regions' sentence. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing enumerable. The page is about exactly one service (AWS WAF) and one rule group within it; it mentions Amazon CloudWatch (metrics for labels) and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (the bot:account and bot:vendor labels) only in passing, and neither is a coverage claim about a service list — a service count of 1, 2 or 3 from this page is meaningless. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The page never lists protected resource types; it says rules run in a 'protection pack (web ACL)' but never enumerates what a web ACL can be associated with (no CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner or Verified Access list appears). What the page DOES give: a rule catalogue (30 rows / 38 named rules) and a bot-category taxonomy (16), both scoped by protection level (19 Common / 19 Targeted by name).

features.collapse: The table names 30 rules, one per row. The count of 38 comes from four rows whose description prose mentions Low, Medium and High variants of the same rule. Those variants are inspection levels named in a sentence, not rows with their own entry, so the published catalogue is the 30 the table names.
features.featureName: Bot Control rules listing (rules in the AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet managed rule group)
features.reasoning: The unit of claim on this page is one named rule inside one managed rule group. The vocabulary has no term for it: 'managedRuleGroup' is the wrong granularity (this whole page is a single managed rule group), 'ipsRule' belongs to Network Firewall's Suricata rules, and 'control'/'findingType' belong to other services' catalogues. So managedRuleName is a NEW camelCase axis name invented for this page, as the brief allows. It is a catalogue axis: the list exists only because AWS publishes it about its own rule group, and the page itself says the authoritative machine-readable list comes from DescribeManagedRuleGroup, and that this documentation covers only the most recent static version.
features.scope: Protection level, stated in the 'Protection levels' section and encoded in the rule names: rules whose name begins with TGT_ are Targeted-level, everything else is Common-level. By rows: 19 Common (16 Category*, 3 Signal*) + 11 Targeted (TGT_*) = 30. By rule names: 19 Common + 19 Targeted (7 single TGT_ rows + 4 x 3 tiered rows = 19) = 38. A second, narrower scope sits inside Targeted: the three TGT_ML_CoordinatedActivity* rules only run when machine learning is enabled in the rule group configuration, which the page says is on by default but can be turned off. No Region, account, plan or resource-type scope appears.
features.statuses: No status column exists. 30 rows / 38 rule names, all present = supported; 0 stated as unsupported; 0 Partial. 30 = 30 present, 0 absent. Not-supported is never stated anywhere on this page — there is no No column, no 'isn't available' sentence, and no exclusion note about rules that do not exist. The per-row 'Rule action' text (Block, Count, CAPTCHA, or a Low/Medium/High action list) is a behaviour attribute of a supported rule, NOT a coverage status; reading Count as 'partial' or Block as 'yes' would be an invention.

features.featureName: Bot categories classified by Bot Control (the Category* rules and the bot:category: labels)
features.reasoning: The category taxonomy is a genuine second coverage statement: it answers 'which kinds of bot does Bot Control name and classify', which is a different question from 'which rules does the rule group contain'. It is derived from the same 16 Category* table rows, so it MUST NOT be added to the 38 of the first feature — a consumer that wants one number per page should use the first feature. threatCategory is the closest vocabulary fit; the values are a taxonomy AWS publishes about its own detections, hence catalogue, not external.
features.scope: All 16 are Common-level (none carries the TGT_ prefix). A behavioural sub-scope, not a coverage status: 15 of the 16 rules state 'Rule action, applied only to unverified bots: Block' and do not match verified bots, while CategoryAI states it applies the Block action to all matches, verified or not. That 15/1 split is about verified-bot handling, not about whether a category is covered.
features.statuses: 16 categories, all present = supported; 0 stated as unsupported; 0 Partial. 16 = 16. In table order: advertising, archiver, content_fetcher, email_client, http_library, link_checker, miscellaneous, monitoring, page_preview, scraping_framework, search_engine, security, seo, social_media, webhooks, ai. Each is stated twice — once as a rule name (CategoryAdvertising ... CategoryAI) and once as the label value awswaf:managed:aws:bot-control:bot:category:<value>. The page names no category that Bot Control does not classify.

pageTitle: AWS WAF Bot Control rule group
shouldNotExtract: The console-experience banner at the top; the VendorName/Name/WCU line (WCU 50 is a capacity figure, not coverage); the three repeated Note blocks about static versions, deliberately limited rule documentation, and contacting AWS Support (they appear twice, verbatim, before the intro and before the rules table); the pricing note and the best-practices/ML-model-update paragraphs. The whole 'Labels added by this rule group' section is reference material about output vocabulary, not a coverage claim, and its sub-lists are the biggest false-positive magnets: the 2 token namespace prefixes (awswaf:managed:token:, awswaf:managed:captcha:); the 3 token status label names (accepted, rejected, absent) and the 4 rejected reasons (not_solved, expired, domain_mismatch, invalid); the 2 special token labels (client session id, browser fingerprint); the ~9 Bot Control bot: label kinds (name, category, account, web_bot_auth, organization, verified, vendor, user_triggered:verified, developer_platform:verified, unverified); the 4 web_bot_auth statuses (verified, invalid, expired, unknown_bot); the 4 cloud-service-provider example values (aws, gcp, azure, oracle); and the signal-label examples, which the page explicitly labels 'not an exhaustive list' and so can never be a count. Also exclude the example bot names (slurp, googlebot, pocket_parser, GoogleBot), the 2 protection levels and the TGT_/TGT_ML_ prefix bullets (configuration, and a scope for the rules feature rather than a feature of their own), the Low/Medium/High numeric thresholds inside the tiered rows (more than 2/5/8 IPs, more than 1/2/3 countries, more than 1/2/3 ASNs, 5 requests in 5 minutes), all cross-reference links, and the trailing 'See also — Skills for AI coding assistants' boilerplate with its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting the 30 table rows and calling it 30 rules. Four rows each pack three comma-separated tier rules into one cell (TGT_ML_CoordinatedActivity{Low,Medium,High}, TGT_TokenReuseIp{...}, TGT_TokenReuseCountry{...}, TGT_TokenReuseAsn{...}), so the honest rule count is 38 and the honest row count is 30 — a parser must state which one it means. Runners-up: (1) harvesting the 'Labels added by this rule group' bullet tree as if it were coverage, which yields a large, unstable, and explicitly non-exhaustive number (the signal labels are prefaced 'This is not an exhaustive list'); (2) reading the per-rule 'Rule action' values as a tri-state — treating Count as Partial and Block as Yes — when they describe how a supported rule behaves, not whether it is supported; (3) inferring a No anywhere, for example from 'For verified bots, the rule group does not match this rule', which is a matching condition, not an unsupported capability; (4) double-counting the 16 Category* rows by adding the bot-category feature to the rule feature; (5) taking WCU 50 or the Low/Medium/High thresholds (2/5/8, 1/2/3) as counts; (6) attributing a Region or resource-type number to a page that states neither.
whatThePageStates: The page documents one AWS Managed Rules rule group, AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet (WCU 50). It has four content sections: 'Protection levels' (two levels, Common and Targeted, with the TGT_ and TGT_ML_ naming conventions), 'Considerations for using this rule group' (pricing and ML-model prose), 'Labels added by this rule group' (token-management labels shared across intelligent threat mitigation, plus the Bot Control label namespace with bot name/category/organization/vendor/account/web_bot_auth/verified/unverified labels and signal-label examples that the page explicitly calls non-exhaustive), and 'Bot Control rules listing' — a two-column table (Rule name, Description) of 30 rows naming 38 rules. The only enumeration on the page that is a real coverage claim is that rules table, plus the bot-category taxonomy the Category* rules name. Every row is a rule that exists; the page never states that anything is NOT covered, and the rule table has no status column at all.
